_comment: The bot population of the Icebreaker slot: scav waves and boss spawns. The `suburbs` stub ships two placeholder waves and zero boss spawns, so before this file the map was empty of everything except whatever another mod put on it.
_whyThisIsAuthorable: A wave record and a boss-spawn record carry NO world coordinates. They name a bot zone by string (`SpawnPoints`, `BossZone`), a role, a count and a time window, and the client resolves the zone name against the BotZone components in the scene. `ZoneIcebreaker` is the zone name upstream's own config declares in `openZones`, so a wave that names it is correct by construction rather than by guesswork. This is the difference between this file and `SpawnPointParams`, which is coordinates and is therefore not shippable here at all -- see README.md.
_sizing: Tuned against a 50-minute raid on a ship: tight interior, few flanks, so fewer bodies than Shoreline and more pressure than Factory. Sum of slots_max is 34 across 11 waves, against a BotMax of 24. That ratio is deliberate -- waves overlap, and a wave table that sums under the cap can never reach it.

waves._note: Opening pressure, both ends of the ship.
A marksman early, because a ship has long sight lines down its own deck and nothing else on this map uses them.
A group rather than singles: the corridors are where a squad is actually frightening.
Mid-raid raiders. This is the wave that makes the ship worth the trip.
Late raiders, timed against the point where a player is committed to an extract rather than exploring.

_bosses: Boss spawns for the slot, in the field names a real database uses -- `BossDifficult`, `BossEscortDifficult`, `BossPlayer`, `RandomTimeSpawn`, NOT the `BossDifficulty`/`IsBossPlayer` spellings that look right and deserialise to nothing. All 140 BossLocationSpawn records in a stock database agree on these.

bossLocationSpawn._note: Rogues holding the bridge. Off by default in config.json (`bossSpawns: false`) because a boss on a map whose loot tables are empty is a fight for nothing.
